youtube.baslik: If one ear hears nothing, what percentage does the calculation give? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In the 1979 method of the American Academy of Otolaryngology (AAO-1979), the binaural rating multiplies the better ear percentage by five, adds the poorer ear percentage and divides the total by six. In an example calculation where one ear is normal and the other has a total loss, the result is about 16.7 percent, that is, one sixth; official ratings are set by the regulations in force.

cumleler: If one ear hears nothing, what percentage does the calculation give?
This example uses the method of the American Academy of Otolaryngology.
Better ear times five, plus the poorer ear, divided by six.
Example: one ear is normal, the other has a total loss.
The result is about sixteen point seven percent, or one in six.
Difficulty in noise and localization is not fully reflected in this number.
